paper.title: Be More Diverse than the Most Diverse: Optimal Mixtures of Generative Models via Mixture-UCB Bandit Algorithms

settings.name_in_paper: Mixture multi-armed bandit with quadratic loss (online selection of optimal mixtures)
unmapped: Objective is a quadratic loss L(P_hat_T) = E[kappa(X,X')] + E[f(X)] of the empirical distribution of all T samples (cross terms between rounds), with kappa a bounded PSD kernel; comparator is the optimal mixture of arms rather than the best single arm
Each pull returns a sample in a general space X (not a scalar reward)
settings.definition_quote: At time $t=1,\ldots,T$, we choose and pull an arm $b^{(t)}\in[m]$ (i.e., generate a sample from model $b^{(t)}$), and obtain a sample $x^{(t)}$ from the distribution $P_{b^{(t)}}$. ... here we minimize the loss $L(\hat{P}^{(T)})$ which involve cross terms $\kappa(x^{(s)},x^{(t)})$ between samples at different rounds.

symbols.Delta_L: sensitivity 2*Delta_kappa + Delta_f, where Delta_kappa, Delta_f are the ranges of kappa and f

conditions: kappa: X^2 -> [kappa_0, kappa_1] positive semidefinite and f: X -> [f_0, f_1] bounded

source.label: thm:alg_converge
source.quote: Suppose $m \ge 2$, $\beta\ge4$. Consider bounded quadratic loss function (\ref{eq:general_loss}) with $\kappa$ being positive semidefinite. Let $\hat{P}^{(T)}$ be the empirical distribution of the first $T\ge2$ samples $\mathbf{x}^{(T)}$ given by Mixture-UCB-CAB. Then the gap between the expected loss and the optimal loss is bounded by \mathbb{E}\big[L(\hat{P}^{(T)})\big]-\min_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}L(\boldsymbol{\alpha}) \le4\Delta_{L}\sqrt{\frac{\beta m\log T}{T}}.

results.notes: Paper bounds the average regret per round (quadratic generalization); multiplied by T here. Comparator is the optimal mixture alpha* (best fixed mixed action), reduces to standard pseudo-regret when kappa=0. Paper's m = number of arms K. Proof gives improved constant 3.382.
